narrative.overview:
The lines are a policy agreed in advance, and the weekly brief is the dated statement of where each one stands. The page is that statement, printed on pale green-grey safety paper in a green-black ink, and its one ornament is the record itself: a full-bleed engraved band under the navigation of every route, drawn from every month-end reading since January 2012. Everything below the band is a document, read top to bottom: the guidance, the five areas, the two scores, then the sections that explain them.

The world borrows the discipline of credit agreements and security printing: structure is the only ornament, every engraved line is drawn from data, each line and tick names itself where it sits, and nothing decorative is added. It refuses the dark data panel with glowing accents, and its opposite, the cream editorial page with an italic serif masthead. "Covenant" names the world for contributors; it never appears in reader copy, and no reader term was minted for it.

Light is the identity; dark is the second theme, the same paper with the lights off. With no stored choice the device setting picks the theme, and a stored choice wins (`app/layout.tsx`, the theme bootstrap). With scripts off, the stylesheet's base draws, which is the dark `:root` block.
keyCharacteristics: One field of colour at page scale: the record band. Everything else is ink on paper.
Two voices: Besley binds, Archivo explains.
Ruled sheets, not cards: hairlines, a 2px ink rule over a list, small radii.
Every drawing puts the easier side up or to the right.
A quiet week has no motion.

rules.name: The Two Meanings Rule
rules.body: A hue on the page is a condition or a crossed line. Anything else is ink. A caveat (cached sources, a scoring note, an archived week, guidance held back) is ink with an outlined diamond, never red: shape carries the state where hue cannot.

rules.name: The Ink Is the Action Rule
rules.body: Links, buttons, focus rings, the selected pill and the caret are the ink in every week. A condition's colour means the condition and nothing else.

rules.name: The One Field Rule
rules.body: Colour commits at page scale in one place, the record band. The condition word beside the guidance is the only other coloured element on the first screen. The regime atmosphere wash is off (`--atmosphere-*: transparent`), because a wash would tint the paper the band is printed on.

rules.name: The Binding Voice Rule
rules.body: Besley sets what the page commits to: the guidance, the condition word, area names, score figures, headings and the wordmark. Archivo sets everything that explains. The voice reaches the page through real rules only (`:where(h1, h2)`, `.type-section`, `.text-display`, `.type-stamp`, `.type-figure`); there is no `font-display` utility.

rules.name: The Type Step Rule
rules.body: Every step is at least 1.125x the one below it at both ends of the range (`tests/typeSteps.test.tsx`). Two sizes closer than that read as one job set twice.

rules.name: The One Number, One Face Rule
rules.body: A figure in a sentence or beside its label stays in its voice with `tabular-nums`. Mono is for a column, a before/after pair or a rail's own labels. A figure that appears on more than one surface is the same figure everywhere.

rules.name: The Measure Rule
rules.body: Prose stops at 60ch, about 75 characters in Archivo, from a base-layer rule on `p` and on list items holding text; a utility on the element overrides it, and a flex or grid row is exempt.

rules.name: The Flat Paper Rule
rules.body: A container is a ruled sheet. If it needs a shadow to separate, it needs a hairline instead.

dos: Do name a condition with `data-regime` and read `--regime-accent` or `--regime-ink`; never type a condition hex at the call site.
Do draw links, buttons and focus rings in the ink, with links underlined.
Do set the guidance, condition word, area names, score figures, headings and wordmark in Besley, and everything that explains in Archivo.
Do separate sheets with a hairline and a step of tone, and lists with a 2px ink rule over hairline rows.
Do give every condition a pattern as well as a fill wherever it fills an area, so the drawing survives greyscale and colour-vision deficiency.
Do label each line and tick where it sits, and keep the easier side up or to the right.
Do keep red for a crossed line, always with a glyph and a word.
Do keep the record band's two records apart: fields are month-end readings scored today; marks are briefs as published.
donts: Don't put a shadow on a container, or a card inside a card.
Don't use a condition's colour for a control, a section label or a page wash.
Don't add a hue that is neither a condition nor a crossed line; a caveat is ink with a diamond.
Don't add a legend where a label in place will do.
Don't add a decorative mark the record did not draw.
Don't set Chivo Mono for a figure that does not align with another.
Don't set a word under 12px, set italics, or type capitals outside a badge.
Don't hand-pick a z-index that can meet a global layer.
